answer: An agent economy can blunt a Sybil attack with a superlinear stake bond: each identity locks collateral, and the bond rises with the square of how many identities one key controls. A lone honest agent pays a tiny delta at the base level, but every extra fake account climbs to a costlier terrace, so an attacker wanting a thousand votes must lock a thousand-squared deposit. Stolen reputation cannot bridge around this, since the bond is re-verified on one ledger each epoch. The attacker's cost grows quadratically while each vote stays worth the same, so flooding the tally never pays.
